[[Category:Educational psychology]]
'''Cognitive load theory (CLT)''' is a theory in [[educational psychology]] describing the impacts of various learning tasks, notably the act of processing information, on the cognitive performance of learners and thereby the learning result.

== Types ==

[[Source:Cognitive load theory, educational research, and instructional design: some food for thought (Scholarly article)|name-author]] recognises 3 types of cognitive loads:<ref>{{#cite:Q3005}}</ref>

* Intrinsic load: related to the inherent difficulty of subject
** i.e., effort required to make sense of concepts
** modelled by [[relational complexity theory]]<ref>{{#cite:Q3028}}</ref>
* Extraneous load: related to material and method
** i.e., effort required to understand a particular presentation of a subject
** filter irrelevant information > strategic semantic understanding<ref>{{#cite:Q3028}}</ref>
* Germane load: related to mental schema construction activities
** i.e., effort required for drawing mental ontological connection to other subjects and internalise new concepts

== Physiological underlying ==

[[File:Cognitive load EEG results.png|thumbnail|500px]]
[[File:ANOVA result cognitive load.png|thumbnail|500px]]
According to results from [[Source:Neural Mechanisms Underlying Intrinsic and Extraneous Cognitive Loads in Numerical Inductive Reasoning (Scholarly article)|name-author]]:

'''Intrinsic cognitive load''' solicits 

* N200: pattern detection
* LPC: [[working memory]] updating
* LNC: relational integration

'''Extraneous cognitive load''' solicits

* P200: Attentional allocation to task-irrelevant stimuli

'''Extraneous+intrinsic cognitive loads''' solicits

* N400: strategic semantic processing

<ref>{{#cite:Q3028}}</ref>

== Limitations ==

Cognitive load theory is a conceptual model of human learning useful for learning design. However, the distinction and underlying physiological responses to different cognitive loads have not yet been fully understood.<ref>{{#cite:Q3005}}</ref>
